prompt: What does JSX let you write?

SQL statements embedded directly in components
Templates containing only static CSS rules
WebAssembly binaries compiled by the browser

prompt: Which hook adds local state to a function component?

useEffect
useRef
useMemo

prompt: How does a parent pass data to a child component?
options: Through props
Through global variables
By mutating the child
Through the DOM only

prompt: What should each item in a rendered list have?

An index attribute that changes after reordering
A ref object shared across every list item
A class component wrapping each rendered value
explanation: Keys let React match list items across renders.

prompt: Which hook runs side effects after render?
options: useEffect
useState
useContext
useId

prompt: How do you render a component named Card?

Card()
new Card()
{Card}

prompt: What must a component name start with to be treated as a component?
options: An uppercase letter
A lowercase letter reserved for custom components
An underscore followed by the component name
A numeric prefix identifying the component type

onclick="handleClick()"
on:click={handleClick}
click={handleClick}

prompt: Which attribute applies a CSS class in JSX?

class
css
styleClass

prompt: How do you embed a JavaScript value in JSX?

Inside a template placeholder: `${value}`
Inside a server tag: `<%= value %>`
Inside square brackets: `[value]`

prompt: What is the virtual DOM?
options: An in-memory representation of the UI
The browser DOM exposed directly to components
A cache containing responses from the application API
A CSS engine that computes the final page layout
explanation: React diffs a lightweight virtual DOM to compute minimal real-DOM updates.

prompt: How do you render multiple elements without adding an extra DOM node?
options: Use a Fragment (<>...</>)
Wrap them in a div always
Return an array of strings
Use a portal
explanation: Fragments group children without rendering a wrapper element.

prompt: Props in React are…
options: Read-only inputs passed to a component
Mutable variables owned locally by the component
Shared state available automatically to every component
DOM attributes that cannot contain JavaScript values

prompt: How do you write inline styles in JSX?

`style="color: red"` using an HTML style string
`css={{ color: 'red' }}` using a built-in css prop
`class="color-red"` using the HTML class attribute

prompt: How do you conditionally render an element when `show` is true?

<if show><Panel /></if>
[show] <Panel />
if (show) <Panel /> inside JSX

items.map(i =>
  • {i.name}
    • )
for (i of items) <li>
<list source={items} />
items.forEach returning JSX directly into the tree

prompt: How do you update state created by useState?
options: Call the setter function returned by useState
Assign a new value directly to the state variable
Mutate the current value without calling its setter
Call useEffect with the new value as a dependency
explanation: useState returns `[value, setValue]`; call the setter to update.

prompt: A controlled input ties its value to…
options: Component state
The input's DOM state without an onChange handler
A localStorage entry read during every render
A CSS custom property bound to the value attribute
explanation: Controlled inputs derive their value from state and update via onChange.

prompt: What does a default export let you do?
options: Import the component under any name
Import only by its exact name
Auto-register the component globally
Skip importing it
explanation: A default export can be imported with any local name.

prompt: How do you stop a form's default submit behavior?
options: Call `event.preventDefault()` in the submit handler
Return false from the component's render function
Call a React-specific `event.stop()` method
Remove the submit handler from the form element

prompt: What value does `<button disabled />` set the disabled prop to?
options: the boolean true
the boolean false
the string disabled
the value undefined
explanation: A boolean prop with no value is shorthand for `true`.

prompt: When is a useState initial value used?
options: When the component state is initialized
Before every render of the component
Only when an effect first reads the state
After the component has completed its first effect
explanation: The initial value seeds state on the first render; later renders keep the current value.

prompt: What kind of object does a React event handler receive?
options: A synthetic event
The raw DOM event always
A Promise
Nothing
explanation: React wraps native events in a cross-browser SyntheticEvent.

prompt: Can React components be written as both functions and classes?
options: Yes, as either function or class components
No, React supports only class components
No, React components must be plain objects
No, React components must be generator functions
explanation: Both are valid; function components with hooks are the modern default.

prompt: What API mounts a React 18 app to the DOM?

`React.start(container, <App />)` from the React package
`ReactDOM.run(container, <App />)` from react-dom
`mount(container, <App />)` as a browser global

prompt: How do you pass children to a component?
options: Place them between the component's opening and closing tags
Set a manually named child prop on every component
Publish them through Context instead of nesting JSX
Register them globally before rendering the parent
explanation: Nested JSX becomes the component's `children` prop.

prompt: What does the key prop primarily help React do?
options: Preserve list-item identity between renders
Apply shared visual styles to every item in a list
Sort list items into the order specified by each key
Cache network requests issued while rendering the list
explanation: Keys give list items stable identity across renders.

prompt: What does a function component return to describe UI?
options: React elements, commonly expressed as JSX
A browser DOM node created directly by the component
An HTML string that React inserts without parsing
No value because React reads the function's local variables
explanation: Components return React elements that React renders to the DOM.

prompt: Where can you declare local variables used by the returned JSX?
options: In the component body before its return statement
Only inside expression braces in the returned JSX
Only in a separate module imported by the component
Inside a key prop attached to the returned element
explanation: Compute values in the body, then reference them in JSX.

prompt: What does onChange on an input let you do?
options: Handle edits and update the input's state
Apply visual styles whenever the input receives focus
Submit the surrounding form after every keystroke
Memoize the current input value between component renders
explanation: onChange fires on input, letting you keep state in sync.

prompt: What does useEffect's dependency array control?
options: When React re-runs the effect
The order in which React registers all component hooks
Which props React passes into the component function
The elements included in the component's rendered output
explanation: The effect re-runs whenever a listed dependency changes.

prompt: What does useMemo do?
options: Caches a computed value between renders
Caches a callback function without invoking it
Runs an external side effect after the browser paints
Creates a mutable ref whose updates persist across renders
explanation: useMemo caches a computed result, recomputing only when deps change.

prompt: What does useCallback return?
options: A memoized function
A cached result produced by immediately calling the function
A mutable object intended for imperative DOM access
The current value read from the nearest Context provider
explanation: useCallback returns the same function reference until its deps change.

prompt: What causes a component to re-render?
options: A state update, a changed prop, or a parent render
Only a full reload of the browser document
Calling useMemo with an unchanged dependency list
Changing a ref's current value inside an event handler
explanation: State/prop changes and parent re-renders trigger re-renders.

prompt: What does useReducer help manage?
options: State transitions expressed through a reducer
HTTP response caching shared across browser tabs
CSS custom properties applied to nested components
Imperative references to browser DOM elements
explanation: useReducer centralizes related state updates in a reducer.

prompt: What does 'lifting state up' mean?
options: Moving shared state to the nearest common ancestor
Copying shared values into module-level global variables
Saving component state as attributes on DOM elements
Caching user state permanently on the application server
explanation: Shared state lives in a common parent that passes it down.

prompt: What problem does Context solve?
options: Sharing values deeply without passing props through every level
Caching expensive calculations between component renders
Running side effects after a component has committed
Combining multiple state updates into a single render
explanation: Context shares values across a subtree without threading props.

prompt: When does a useEffect cleanup function run?
options: Before the effect runs again and when the component unmounts
Only when the component performs its initial mount
Only after the component has been removed from the DOM
After every render, even when the effect did not re-run
explanation: Cleanup runs before re-running the effect and when the component unmounts.

prompt: What does an empty dependency array `[]` mean for useEffect?
options: Run after mounting, with cleanup on unmount
Run after every committed render of the component
Skip the effect for the component's entire lifetime
Run synchronously before React renders the component
explanation: With an empty dependency array, an effect is not re-run for dependency changes; its cleanup still runs on unmount. In development, StrictMode may run an extra setup-and-cleanup cycle.

prompt: Why must you not mutate state directly?
options: React may miss the change when the reference stays the same
JavaScript throws whenever an object is mutated
Mutation always consumes more memory than copying data
The browser DOM changes immediately without a React render
explanation: React relies on new references to detect changes; mutation can be missed.

prompt: How should derived data (e.g. a filtered list) be handled?
options: Compute it during render from existing state
Store it in separate state and sync with effects
Put it in a ref
Recompute it in the DOM
explanation: Derive values during render to avoid duplicate, drift-prone state.

prompt: What does useContext return?
options: The value from the nearest matching provider
A newly created Context object for the component
A setter that updates the provider automatically
The provider element associated with the Context
explanation: useContext reads the current value from the closest Provider.

prompt: What's the difference between controlled and uncontrolled inputs?
options: Controlled inputs use React state; uncontrolled inputs retain DOM state
Controlled inputs always render faster than uncontrolled inputs
Uncontrolled inputs require Redux to preserve their values
Both input types keep their source of truth in React state
explanation: Controlled inputs read/write React state; uncontrolled rely on the DOM.

prompt: How can a child update its parent's state?
options: Receive and call a callback passed by the parent
Mutate the parent's state variable through the child instance
Write the new value to an automatically shared global variable
Update it directly without any function supplied by the parent
explanation: Pass a handler down; the child invokes it to update parent state.

prompt: What does React.StrictMode do in development?
options: Re-runs selected logic to expose unsafe side effects
Minifies component code before the development bundle runs
Turns every component into a server-rendered component
Prevents function components from calling React hooks
explanation: StrictMode intentionally double-runs some logic in dev to expose impurities.

prompt: How do you provide lazy initial state to useState?
options: Pass an initializer function to useState
Pass a Promise that resolves to the initial state
Set the initial state from a mount-only useEffect
Call useState without an argument and mutate the result
explanation: An initializer function runs only on the first render.

prompt: Why prefer the functional updater setX(prev => prev + 1)?
options: It calculates from the latest queued state value
React requires updater syntax for every numeric state change
It prevents the component from rendering after the update
It forces React to process the state update synchronously
explanation: The updater receives the current state, avoiding stale captured values.

prompt: What does 'batching' mean for state updates?
options: React processes several queued updates in one render
React sends state updates to the server as one request
React discards all but the final update in an event
React moves state calculations onto a background worker
explanation: React groups updates to minimize renders.

prompt: What is prop drilling?
options: Passing props through components that only forward them
Checking prop values against runtime validation rules
Caching prop objects so their identity remains stable
Copying every received prop onto a child with spread syntax
explanation: Threading props through layers that only forward them is prop drilling.

prompt: How do you forward all received props to a child?
options: <Child {...props} />
<Child props={props} />
<Child spread />
Child.props = props
explanation: Object spread `{...props}` forwards all properties as props.

prompt: Why must hooks be called in the same order every render?
options: React associates each hook's state with its call position
A stable hook order makes JavaScript execute more quickly
Every hook starts an asynchronous task in call order
JSX syntax requires hooks to appear before returned markup
explanation: React associates state with the order hooks are called, so order must be stable.

prompt: What happens when a component's key changes?
options: React replaces the component instance and resets its state
React renders the same instance while preserving all state
React ignores the new key after the component has mounted
React throws because keys cannot change between renders
explanation: A new key makes React treat it as a different element, remounting it.

prompt: What does a Portal let you do?
options: Render children into another DOM container
Load remote data outside the component hierarchy
Cache child elements until their props change
Create a Context provider around the portal's children
explanation: createPortal renders into a DOM node outside the parent hierarchy (e.g. modals).

prompt: When does useEffect run relative to the browser paint?
options: After the browser has painted the committed update
Before React begins rendering the component tree
While React is calculating the component's output
Only before paint, because effects cannot run afterward
explanation: useEffect runs after the browser paints, so it doesn't block visual updates.

prompt: What's the difference between useMemo and useCallback?
options: useMemo caches a value; useCallback caches a function
Both hooks cache and return exactly the same kind of value
useCallback caches a computed value after calling its callback
useMemo schedules side effects after the component commits
explanation: `useCallback(fn, d)` ≈ `useMemo(() => fn, d)`.

prompt: What type should a wrapper component's `children` prop be in TS?
options: `React.ReactNode`
`string`, because children must contain visible text
`JSX.Element`, because a wrapper accepts one element only
`any[]`, because React always normalizes children to arrays
explanation: ReactNode covers elements, strings, arrays, null, etc.

prompt: Why does conditionally calling a hook cause errors?
options: It changes the hook call positions React uses for state
JavaScript syntax forbids function calls in conditional blocks
It forces React to render every component exactly twice
It mutates the component's props before hooks can read them
explanation: Skipping a hook on some renders desyncs React's internal hook list.

prompt: What does the dependency lint rule 'exhaustive-deps' warn about?

Dependency arrays containing more than three values
Imported modules that are unused by the component
Rendered list elements that do not have stable keys
explanation: It flags reactive values referenced but not listed as dependencies.

{if loading <a/> else <b/>}
<switch>
[loading]<a/><b/>

prompt: What is reconciliation?
options: Comparing element trees to determine DOM updates
A library for storing global application state
Rendering React components into an HTML string on a server
A styling approach that scopes CSS rules to components
explanation: Reconciliation compares element trees to compute minimal DOM changes.

prompt: What does useRef provide?
options: A mutable object that persists without triggering renders
Reactive state that schedules a render whenever it changes
A cached calculation recomputed from a dependency list
The current value supplied by the nearest Context provider
explanation: useRef's `.current` survives renders and changing it doesn't re-render.

prompt: What is a core rule of hooks?
options: Call hooks at the top level in a consistent order
Call hooks inside loops when rendering repeated elements
Call hooks from event handlers after user interactions
Wrap hook calls in try/catch to handle rendering errors
explanation: Top-level, unconditional calls keep hook order stable.

prompt: What does React.memo do?
options: Can skip a render when props are shallowly equal
Caches requests made by the component across renders
Memoizes an arbitrary calculation and returns its value
Creates a mutable reference to the wrapped component
explanation: React.memo bails out of re-render if props haven't shallow-changed.

prompt: Why must you treat state as immutable?
options: A new reference helps React detect a state change
JavaScript prohibits mutation of objects stored in variables
Immutable values always consume less memory than mutable ones
Refs can store only objects that have never been mutated
explanation: New references signal change; in-place mutation can be missed.

prompt: What is a custom hook?
options: A function that composes hooks to share stateful logic
A class method that replaces a component lifecycle method
A Context provider that automatically stores global state
A component wrapper that modifies another component's props
explanation: Custom hooks (use…) extract reusable hook-based logic.

prompt: What is a stale closure bug in an effect?

An effect is registered but never executes after a commit
A retained ref object causes the browser to leak memory
Two rendered siblings receive the same reconciliation key

prompt: What does useImperativeHandle customize?
options: The handle exposed through a component's ref
The React elements returned by the component render
The current value distributed by a Context provider
Whether an effect runs before or after browser paint

Only when each consumer performs its initial mount
Never, because Context values are read without rendering
Only when the provider's children prop changes identity

Nest additional providers that all receive new object values
Use array indexes as keys for every Context consumer
Disable StrictMode so development renders happen only once
explanation: Narrower contexts and a stable value reduce consumer churn.

prompt: Why does passing a new object/array prop each render defeat React.memo?
options: Shallow comparison sees a different reference
memo ignores every prop whose value is an object
React does not permit objects or arrays to be passed as props
memo deep-clones object props before comparing their fields

prompt: Why is calling setState directly during render a problem?
options: It can trigger an endless sequence of renders
JavaScript syntax forbids calling functions during rendering
It prevents all registered effects from running after commit
It directly mutates every prop received by the component
explanation: Updating state in render schedules another render, looping.

prompt: What do Error Boundaries catch?
options: Render and lifecycle errors in descendant components
Exceptions thrown from event handlers after rendering
Rejected promises from arbitrary asynchronous callbacks
Every failed HTTP request made anywhere in the subtree
explanation: Error boundaries catch render/lifecycle errors below them, not async/handler errors.

prompt: What does useLayoutEffect let you do that useEffect doesn't?
options: Measure or change layout before the browser paints
Schedule work only after the browser has painted the update
Fetch remote data with a higher network priority
Run an effect without declaring values it depends on

prompt: What is forwardRef used for?
options: Expose a descendant node or handle through a ref
Cache a component's last output when props are equal
Create a Context and provide its initial shared value
Delay updating a value until urgent rendering has finished
explanation: forwardRef lets a parent attach a ref to something inside a child.

prompt: When should you prefer useReducer over useState?
options: When related state has complex transition logic
Whenever state consists of a single independent boolean
When the goal is to prevent every component re-render
Only when the reducer state is distributed through Context
explanation: useReducer centralizes complex, related transitions.

prompt: How do you declaratively reset a child's internal state?
options: Change its key to remount it
Call a reset() prop hopefully
Mutate its state
Use forceUpdate
explanation: A new key remounts the component, clearing its state.

prompt: What does the render-props pattern enable?
options: Share behavior while the caller chooses the rendered UI
Make the shared component render faster by default
Render the component tree entirely on the server
Memoize every value returned by the render function
explanation: A function-as-child receives state and returns the UI to render.

prompt: Why can using the array index as a key cause bugs on reorder?
options: Reordering changes identity and can attach state to another item
Numeric indexes take longer for React to compare than strings
React requires every key value to be a JavaScript number
An index key disables memoization for the entire parent tree
explanation: Index keys don't track item identity through insertions/reorders.

prompt: What does flushSync do?
options: Forces pending updates to commit synchronously
Defers pending state updates until the browser becomes idle
Cancels state updates queued during the current event
Combines updates scheduled in separate event-loop tasks
explanation: flushSync opts out of batching for a synchronous DOM update (use sparingly).

prompt: Why should components be pure (no side effects during render)?
options: Rendering stays predictable and safe to restart
Pure components must be written as JavaScript classes
Purity prevents components from receiving any props
Pure rendering removes the need for stable list keys
explanation: Pure render lets React render, pause, and replay safely.

prompt: Why might memoizing a child still not prevent re-renders from context?
options: A consumed Context update is independent of prop comparison
memo compares props only for components written as classes
Every Context is global state shared with the whole application
memo caches Context values and prevents consumers updating
explanation: memo compares props; a context value change re-renders consumers regardless.

prompt: What's the risk of an expensive computation directly in the component body?
options: The computation repeats whenever the component renders
React detects the cost and permanently skips the computation
It prevents effects registered by the component from running
It mutates the component's state during reconciliation
explanation: Without useMemo, costly work repeats each render.

prompt: Why is reading a ref's .current inside render discouraged?
options: Ref changes are not reactive, and the node may not be committed
React freezes every ref object while a component renders
Reading current schedules another render of the component
Accessing a ref is slower than reading component state
explanation: Refs are for imperative access in effects/handlers, not render logic.

prompt: What does keying inputs in a dynamic list prevent?
options: Local state and DOM identity moving to a different row
Keyboard input events taking longer to reach the handler
CSS selectors from one list row applying to every sibling
Repeated rows issuing duplicate requests to the network
explanation: Stable keys keep each row's DOM/state tied to its data.

prompt: Why do new function identities each render matter for hooks?
options: They can invalidate memoized props and effect dependencies
Each new function remains allocated forever and leaks memory
A function prop blocks React from rendering its child
JavaScript prohibits creating functions inside another function
explanation: Recreated closures change references, affecting memo/deps comparisons.

prompt: What is a Higher-Order Component (HOC)?
options: A function that accepts a component and returns another component
A hook that may be called outside a React component
A Context provider created without a matching consumer
A class lifecycle method that wraps the render method
explanation: HOCs wrap components to add behavior (a pre-hooks reuse pattern).

prompt: Why prefer deriving state during render over syncing with an effect?
options: It avoids an extra render and duplicated state that can drift
Effects are deprecated and unavailable in function components
Calculating derived values during render is always slower
The Rules of Hooks require every value to be derived
explanation: Effect-based syncing causes redundant renders and can drift; derive instead.

prompt: What does a dependency on a derived object in useEffect risk?
options: A new object identity can make the effect run each render
React permanently skips the effect after the initial render
JavaScript reports a syntax error for object dependencies
The dependency forces browser painting to wait for the effect
explanation: A new object reference each render makes the effect fire constantly; memoize it.

prompt: How does React decide to bail out of re-rendering on a state setter call?
options: It compares the next and current state with Object.is
It recursively compares every nested property for equality
It always renders after a setter call, even for equal values
It checks whether the browser DOM changed independently
explanation: If the new state is Object.is-equal to the old, React can skip the re-render.

prompt: What does concurrent rendering (React 18) enable?
options: Rendering that React can pause, prioritize, or discard
JavaScript execution distributed across multiple CPU threads
Server rendering automatically enabled for every component
Updates restricted to one uninterrupted synchronous render
explanation: Concurrent React can pause, resume, and abandon renders by priority.

prompt: What does useTransition do?
options: Marks an update as non-urgent and reports pending status
Animates DOM changes produced by a state update
Defers a prop value received from code outside your control
Forces an update to render and commit synchronously
explanation: useTransition lets urgent updates interrupt lower-priority transition updates.

prompt: How does useLayoutEffect differ from useEffect?
options: It runs after DOM changes but before browser paint
It runs during server rendering to calculate layout
It always runs after the browser has painted the update
It registers an effect that cannot return a cleanup function
explanation: useLayoutEffect blocks paint, suiting layout measurement/sync mutations.

prompt: What do React Server Components primarily reduce?
options: JavaScript sent to the client and client-side data fetching
The amount of CPU time consumed by the application server
The number of CSS rules included in the rendered page
The number of hooks called by interactive components
explanation: RSCs render on the server, shipping less JS and fetching data server-side.

prompt: Why can a key like the array index cause bugs?
options: Insertions change identity and can move state to another item
A sufficiently large numeric index overflows React's key storage
React accepts string keys but rejects all numeric key values
Using an index key disables Suspense for the containing list
explanation: Index keys misrepresent identity across list mutations.

prompt: What problem does useSyncExternalStore solve?
options: Consistent subscriptions to external stores during concurrent rendering
A faster alternative to Context for every shared application value
Fetching server data before a component begins rendering
Synchronizing animation frames with React state updates
explanation: It guarantees consistent reads from external stores during concurrent renders.

prompt: What is 'tearing' in concurrent React?
options: Components show inconsistent snapshots of shared data
A component retains an object after it has unmounted
Hydration stops because the server returned invalid markup
A style update appears one frame later than expected
explanation: Interruptible rendering can show mismatched snapshots of an external store — tearing.

prompt: What changed about batching in React 18 (automatic batching)?
options: React also batches updates from promises, timers, and native events
React removed batching so every setter renders immediately
React batches updates from class components but not functions
Applications must explicitly enable batching for event handlers
explanation: React 18 batches updates outside React event handlers too.

prompt: What does Suspense do for data/code that isn't ready?
options: Shows a fallback until a descendant is ready
Stores completed HTTP responses in a shared data cache
Memoizes all descendants until their props change
Prevents the suspended subtree from ever rendering again
explanation: Suspense renders a fallback while a descendant suspends loading.

prompt: What does the 'use client' directive mark?
options: A client boundary whose exports may use client features
A module that React guarantees will execute only on the server
A component automatically wrapped in React.memo
A dynamic import that is excluded from the initial bundle
explanation: 'use client' opts a module into client-side rendering/interactivity.

prompt: Why can't React Server Components use useState?
options: They execute on the server and have no interactive client state
React deprecated useState when Server Components were introduced
Every Server Component must be written as a JavaScript class
Their state is stored globally instead of per component instance
explanation: RSCs have no client lifecycle, so hooks like useState don't apply.

prompt: What does a hydration mismatch typically cause?
options: A warning and possible replacement of the mismatched server subtree
A faster first paint because React skips hydration work
A retained object that creates a browser memory leak
A stylesheet reset applied to the mismatched element
explanation: Server/client output divergence triggers hydration warnings/repairs.

prompt: What is selective hydration?
options: React hydrates boundaries based partly on user interaction
React hydrates stylesheet links but skips component markup
React leaves all server-rendered HTML permanently unhydrated
React performs the hydration work only on the server
explanation: React 18 can hydrate Suspense boundaries out of order, guided by interaction.

prompt: What does useId generate?
options: An identifier stable across server and client rendering
A random value intended for keys in dynamically reordered lists
A mutable ref object whose current value is the identifier
A new Context instance identified by the generated value
explanation: useId produces SSR-safe unique IDs for accessibility attributes.

prompt: Why is double-invoking effects in StrictMode (dev) useful?
options: It reveals effects that lack cleanup or safe repeatability
It reduces production render time by warming component caches

Deploy configuration changes without keeping a rollback

Rewrite all source imports as part of the first migration

Read private server secrets directly from browser code

Bundle server credentials into shared browser constants

Repeat all source transformations after every file change

Polyfill every known API without defining browser targets

Remove content hashes to make caching appear stable
Assume config changes cannot affect emitted file content

When every workload needs the fastest cold build
Only when applications cannot use ES modules

prompt: What is pnpm?

A TypeScript source compiler

options: Reusing files from a shared store
One compressed runtime archive
Deleting all dev dependencies
Never storing downloaded files

pnpm.config

prompt: What is Corepack?

A package registry
A monorepo task scheduler

prompt: What defines a pnpm workspace?
options: pnpm-workspace.yaml
workspace.config.json
package-lock.json
package.json scripts

prompt: How does pnpm's default isolated layout help catch undeclared imports?
options: It exposes fewer undeclared dependencies
It flattens all transitive packages
It hides every peer dependency
It compiles one combined module
explanation: Direct dependencies are linked into the project's node_modules. Private hoisting and workspace-root resolution still exist, so this layout is not an absolute isolation boundary.

prompt: What does `pnpm --filter` do?
options: Selects packages for a command
Filters allowed licenses
Deletes matching dependencies
Filters versions by release date

prompt: What does Corepack pin via the packageManager field?
options: The package manager and its version
The Node.js runtime version
The registry authentication method
The OS and architecture
explanation: An exact packageManager value such as pnpm@11.2.0 lets Corepack select that manager version; it does not select the Node.js runtime.

prompt: How can pnpm avoid the cost of repeatedly copying dependency files?
options: Links or clones avoid repeated file copies
It skips globally installed packages
It deletes package resource files
It downloads dependencies on demand
explanation: When supported, linking or copy-on-write cloning from the store avoids repeatedly copying identical bytes. Actual install time also includes resolution, downloads, and scripts.

prompt: What does the workspace: protocol do in a monorepo?
options: Requires a local workspace dependency
Prefers the registry version
Pins the current Git commit
Declares a peer dependency
explanation: workspace:* resolves to the local package rather than the registry.

prompt: What are phantom dependencies, and how does pnpm reduce accidental access to them?
options: Undeclared imports; isolated links reduce them
Unversioned releases; adds versions
Import cycles; removes cycles
Optional packages; blocks them
explanation: Phantom dependencies are imported without being declared. The isolated layout reduces accidental access, but hoisting and root dependencies can still make undeclared packages reachable.

prompt: How does the content-addressable store dedupe across projects?
options: Identical file content shares store storage
Compresses each project's packages
Keeps only the newest version
Links every file to the registry
explanation: The store addresses files by content, allowing identical data to be reused. Physical sharing depends on the selected import method and filesystem.

prompt: How does pnpm handle peer dependencies?
options: It tracks resolved peer contexts
It always installs the latest peer
It merges all peer versions
It rejects every peer conflict
explanation: Peer contexts can require separate package instances. Missing compatible peers may be auto-installed; strictPeerDependencies defaults to false, so peer problems need not fail installation.

prompt: What does `pnpm dlx` do?
options: Fetches and runs a package's executable
Adds a permanent dev dependency
Prints installed package licenses
Links an existing workspace
explanation: dlx fetches and runs a CLI package on the fly (like npx).

prompt: Why avoid publicly hoisting every dependency into the application root?
options: To limit undeclared application imports
To disable CommonJS support
To eliminate node_modules
To replace all peer dependencies
explanation: Public hoisting makes undeclared imports easier. pnpm's isolated layout can still use private hoisting inside the virtual store; it does not disable all hoisting by default.

prompt: How do hard links affect install speed and disk usage?
options: Multiple paths share the same file data
Every path contains a copy
Reads fetch from the registry
Adding a link copies the file
explanation: Hard links reference the same file data instead of allocating another complete copy. They require compatible filesystem locations; other import methods may be used when unavailable.

prompt: What team problem does Corepack solve?
options: Package-manager version drift
Browser support differences
Shared-source syntax errors
Lost dependency lockfiles
explanation: A pinned manager and a consistent Corepack setup reduce install-tool drift. They do not replace the dependency lockfile or runtime pin.

prompt: What does `pnpm store prune` do?
options: Removes unreferenced store content
Deletes all project installations
Deletes lockfile resolutions
Uninstalls Corepack managers
explanation: Pruning removes unreferenced store packages. A later install may need to fetch those packages again.

prompt: Why does pnpm's strictness improve correctness in monorepos?
options: It exposes missing dependency declarations
It adds missing declarations
It merges every package
It disables peer resolution
explanation: Fewer exposed transitive packages makes missing declarations easier to detect. Each workspace package should declare its own direct dependencies.

prompt: How does Corepack provision a package manager on first use?
options: Downloads and caches the selected version
Recompiles it for every command
Bundles every version with Node
Requires a global manager install
explanation: Corepack can fetch a selected package-manager version and cache it. Offline environments need that version provisioned in advance.

prompt: Which command installs all dependencies with pnpm?

pnpm fetch
pnpm setup
pnpm import

prompt: Which command adds a dependency?

pnpm view <pkg>

pnpm store prune

prompt: Which command updates dependencies?

pnpm rebuild

explanation: Use --latest to ignore ranges.

prompt: Which file lists workspace packages?
options: pnpm-workspace.yaml

workspace.config.js

prompt: Which command displays the installed dependency tree?

prompt: Which command runs a binary from node_modules?

prompt: With Corepack installed, which command creates its package-manager shims?

corepack cache clean

prompt: In pnpm's default isolated layout, what is node_modules/.pnpm?
options: The isolated layout's virtual store
Package-manager configuration
The shared content store
Dependency lifecycle logs
explanation: The virtual store holds package instances and dependency links. It is distinct from the shared content-addressable store.

prompt: Which install flag fails if resolving dependencies would require changing the lockfile?

--lockfile-only
--no-lockfile
--prefer-offline

prompt: Which command checks for outdated packages?

pnpm store status

prompt: Which command shows why a package is installed?

pnpm audit
explanation: Useful for finding duplicate versions.

prompt: Which command initializes a package.json without a starter template?

prompt: Is pnpm compatible with the npm registry?

pnpm store status

prompt: What does pnpm create do?

Rewrites source imports

Builds all dependencies first

An offline-only package store

Files in published tarballs
Registries accepting a token

prompt: What does the catalog feature in pnpm provide?

Copy dependencies into source

prompt: What does allowBuilds control in current pnpm?

Production bundle contents
Task-output cache retention

Watches workspace files

Combines multiple workspace manifests into one file
Removes unused files from the global package store

Every symlink creates a second complete file copy

prompt: How does pnpm's side-effects cache help?

Removes lifecycle scripts from downloaded packages

Turns local packages into registry-only dependencies
Injects environment variables into each package build

prompt: Why enable strictPeerDependencies?

Install all peers at their newest available version
Hoist every peer into the workspace root automatically

prompt: What can cause an ignored dependency-build warning or error?

The lockfile contains an unresolved merge marker

prompt: How does pnpm keep installs consistent across OSes?

The package manager emulates the target OS at runtime
Optional dependencies always bypass platform checks

prompt: Why can mixing package managers in one repo cause problems?

The registry forbids multiple managers in one project
explanation: Managers can resolve and lay out packages differently. Choose and enforce one installation workflow instead of treating lockfiles as interchangeable.

prompt: How do you enforce pnpm usage in a repo?

Delete the lockfile so managers share fresh resolutions
Let CI select whichever manager is installed globally
explanation: Provision the pinned manager and validate it in CI. Corepack's packageManager check does not automatically prevent direct use of an npm executable outside its shims.

prompt: What does resolutionMode influence?

The network concurrency used for package downloads
The filesystem directory used for the shared store
The order of lifecycle scripts during installation
explanation: Resolution modes choose how dependency ranges are resolved, for example preferring lower direct versions or using publication-time constraints.

prompt: Why might a CI install differ from local?

CI inherently resolves every version to the latest

The same lockfile forces identical native builds on all OSes
explanation: Compare runtime and manager versions, configuration, lockfile state, and platform. A frozen lockfile removes one source of drift but not all of them.

prompt: How do you update a transitive dependency with a vulnerability?

Edit installed files without recording a durable patch
Remove the affected dependency from the lockfile only
Suppress advisories while leaving the vulnerable resolution

prompt: What risk does minimumReleaseAge reduce?

Dependencies whose unpacked size exceeds a threshold

prompt: What does workspace topological ordering mean for pnpm -r run?

Every workspace starts simultaneously regardless of graph

prompt: How do you handle private packages with pnpm?

Put registry tokens in committed build command arguments
Copy a developer's complete auth file into public artifacts

prompt: What changed about Corepack distribution starting with Node.js 25?

It became the mandatory installer in Node.js 25
It dropped support for pnpm in favor of npm only
It merged package-manager code into the Node runtime

prompt: How would you set up a large monorepo with pnpm?

Give all apps access to all root dependencies
Use independent lockfiles while assuming one resolution

prompt: How do you migrate a monorepo from npm or Yarn to pnpm?

Rename package-lock.json to pnpm-lock.yaml directly
Retain npm and pnpm lockfiles as interchangeable inputs
Switch the CI command without checking undeclared imports

prompt: How do you keep dependency versions consistent across many packages?

Give each package unrelated unconstrained version ranges
Place every dependency in the root without peer checks
Rely on a shared store to force one dependency version
explanation: Catalogs reuse version ranges across workspace manifests. They simplify updates but do not require every package instance to resolve identically.

prompt: How do you secure the dependency supply chain with pnpm?

Treat a lockfile as proof that every package is trusted
Approve every install script to avoid interactive prompts
Assume store deduplication detects malicious source code
explanation: These controls address different risks: reproducibility, install-time code execution, known advisories, and very recent releases.

prompt: How do you make CI installs fast and reliable?

Use the newest pnpm release without recording its version
Skip lockfile validation whenever the store cache hits
Delete all cached content before every installation
explanation: Caching avoids repeated downloads.

prompt: How do you decide between pnpm, npm and Yarn?
options: Evaluate requirements and compatibility
Choose by registry download totals without testing tools
Assume a smaller lockfile always means faster builds
Select solely by which manager is already global
explanation: Compare the project's supported tools, workspace needs, installation behavior, and team workflow using a representative repository.

prompt: How do you handle a tool that requires a flat node_modules?

Set resolve.alias in the bundler to flatten all installs
Disable peer checking to remove node_modules symlinks
Run store prune to convert the virtual store to flat files

prompt: How do you run only affected packages in CI?

Filter only by package name and ignore dependency edges
Use --prod to select packages changed since main
Use --offline to skip builds for unchanged workspaces

prompt: How do you coordinate releases of many workspace packages?

Publish all workspaces after every documentation change
Give each dependent a fixed version without updating ranges
Rely on pnpm publish to design the release policy itself
explanation: A release tool can coordinate version changes and changelogs; pnpm publishes the prepared package artifacts.

prompt: How do you roll out a pnpm major upgrade to a team?

Upgrade developer machines before changing CI inputs
Keep an old lockfile even when its format is unsupported
Change Node, pnpm, and every dependency without comparison

prompt: How do you design package boundaries in a workspace?

Reach into sibling source trees using relative paths
Allow cyclic imports whenever package names differ
Hide all shared modules in a root-only dependency list
explanation: Clear exports prevent coupling.

prompt: How do you debug slow installs in a large monorepo?

Delete the store before measuring warm installation time
Assume the registry is slow without examining timings
Add build workers without checking the expensive phase
explanation: Install scripts often dominate time.

prompt: How do you manage Node.js versions across a team?

Use packageManager alone to select the Node.js version
Let every contributor use a different runtime major
Treat an engines warning as strict version enforcement

prompt: How do you handle deploying a single app from a monorepo?

Copy the root node_modules symlinks without their targets
Ship only package.json and assume dependencies are global
Exclude local workspace packages from the deployment

prompt: How do you keep a monorepo's root package.json lean?

Declare all runtime dependencies at the workspace root
Make shared build tools dependencies of every application
Remove workspace metadata to avoid a root manifest
explanation: Clear ownership eases upgrades.

prompt: How do you evaluate dependency health before adding a package?
options: Review maintenance, code, and dependencies
Approve any package with a high repository star count
Treat a passing vulnerability scan as a complete review
Judge package health solely by its weekly download total
explanation: Inspect ownership, maintenance, code, dependency cost, and install scripts. Popularity or an advisory scan alone does not establish trust.

prompt: How do you handle Corepack no longer being bundled with Node?
options: Provision Corepack or another pinned setup
Downgrade Node indefinitely to keep bundled shims
Assume packageManager installs its own executable
Run whichever global pnpm happens to be available
explanation: Install Corepack separately or provision an explicitly pinned pnpm version by another supported method. packageManager records a choice but is not an executable installer by itself.

prompt: How do you audit license compliance across a pnpm workspace?
options: Inventory licenses and apply project policy
